products.title: Large Frame
products.subtitle: Dior Maison x Pierre Yovanovitch, Oak Wood

paragraphs: DIOR MAISON X PIERRE YOVANOVITCH Dior Maison's collection of objects designed by Pierre Yovanovitch is the meeting of two stories. On one side, that of the Château de la Colle Noire, a property acquired by Christian Dior in the 1950s in the village of Montauroux in the Var countryside. On the other, that of the Château de Fabrègues, 65 km away, into which Pierre Yovanovitch has breathed new life for the last 10 years. Like Dior, who often stayed in the plains of Callian, Yovanovitch is also a child of the South, born in Nice, with strong ties to this region. In a sense, the collection, consisting of 15 objects including the large frame, is a reflection of this common southern anchorage. The design is 'simple, solid and noble,' as Dior defined his Colle Noire residence. Clean and functional, it celebrates the savoir-faire that Pierre Yovanovitch loves. The collection highlights traditional carpentry techniques and noble assemblies with local and sustainable materials selected for their beauty and timelessness. This collaboration is part of a story written by Dior Maison since the 1970s, featuring the greatest names in contemporary design, with Gabriella Crespi at the forefront. *Design by Pierre Yovanovitch for Dior
bullets: Dior Maison x Pierre Yovanovitch, Oak Wood

paragraphs: An invitation to the sweetness of life, the Dior Maison x Pierre Yovanovitch collection is enhanced by the understated elegance of creations imagined by the interior designer. A series of essentials — trays, trinket trays, candle holders, a pencil holder and tissue boxes — are unveiled in a darker version delicately paired with embossed leather details in new colors. The ultimate surprise, a box containing two decks of cards by Roman artist Pietro Ruffo and a game of dominoes complete the collection of office accessories, offering an intriguing escape. *Design by Pierre Yovanovitch for Dior

products.subtitle: Manufacture des Émaux de Longwy for Dior, Ecru Ceramic and Enamel with Multicolor Granville Floral Motif and Gold

paragraphs: The large round vase is unveiled as part of the Granville collection inspired by the Les Rhumbs Villa, in homage to Mr. Dior's childhood haven. Handcrafted in ecru ceramic and enamel, the vase is embellished with 24-carat gold and features delicate roses in gold, pink and blue hues, blossoming on the ironwork of a winter garden. The enameling process, hand-applied one drop at a time, is extremely precise, displaying outstanding execution. The exceptional creation will infuse any interior with poetic charm and can be coordinated with other pieces from the Granville collection to create a delicate atmosphere. Manufacture des Émaux de Longwy for Dior.
